claims.claim: Adam Roberts's Fantasy: A Short History says Martin lets readers have their chivalric cake and eat it too, thrilling at poisonings, rapes and betrayals while enamoured of noble houses and titles; no sentence-level prose judgment is reported.
claims.source: Stephanie Burt reviewing Adam Roberts, Fantasy: A Short History, Strange Horizons, 2026 (Roberts's judgments as quoted by Burt)
claims.quote: have their chivalric cake and eat it too

claims.claim: The Washington Post's 1996 review faulted one-dimensional characters and less than memorable imagery.
claims.source: Bookmarks Reviews roundup of 1996 reviews of A Game of Thrones (quoting John H. Riskind, Washington Post, 28 Jul 1996)
claims.quote: one-dimensional characters and less than memorable imagery

claims.claim: Dana Jennings's Times review says the book, like all proper serials, gives no emotional respite and ends on razor-sharp question marks.
claims.source: BookBrowse review roundup for A Dance with Dragons (quoting Dana Jennings, New York Times, Jul 2011), read via Wayback
claims.quote: ending with several razor-sharp question marks

claims.claim: Martin's writing is well above average for commercial prose, but he is not a seven-drafts literary reviser.
claims.source: Michael O. Church, 'The Tragedy of George R. R. Martin', Substack, 19 Jun 2025
claims.quote: well above average for commercial prose

claims.claim: Martin says the editing of his novels does not really begin until he delivers the finished novel, at which point his editors read it and give him notes.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, So Spake Martin "Editing Process", westeros.org (2000-02-29)
claims.quote: the editing does not really begin until I deliver the finished novel

claims.claim: Martin says the copyeditor on his novels checks the manuscript for internal consistency among other things.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, So Spake Martin "Editing Process", westeros.org (2000-02-29)
claims.quote: checks it for grammar, syntax, spelling, internal consistancy

claims.claim: Martin says he revises constantly while writing, honing and polishing as he goes rather than submitting finished chapters serially.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, So Spake Martin "Editing Process", westeros.org (2000-02-29)
claims.quote: I revise constantly as I go along, always honing and polishing

claims.claim: Martin says a new idea while writing chapter fifty-two can require him to go back and change chapters three, nine and twenty-one.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, So Spake Martin "Editing Process", westeros.org (2000-02-29)
claims.quote: go back and change chapters three, nine, and twenty-one

claims.claim: Pajiba reports that Martin's editor Anne Groell tried to cut back a repeated phrase in A Dance With Dragons.
claims.source: Genevieve Burgess, Pajiba (2014-05-30), relaying Anne Groell's Suvudu Q&A
claims.quote: The repeated phrase she tried to cut back on

claims.claim: Pajiba reports that the phrase "words are wind" appears 14 times in A Dance With Dragons.
claims.source: Genevieve Burgess, Pajiba (2014-05-30), relaying Anne Groell's Suvudu Q&A

claims.claim: Pajiba reports that Groell's initial edit of A Dance With Dragons took two weeks, most of it spent back-checking information from previous books.
claims.source: Genevieve Burgess, Pajiba (2014-05-30), relaying Anne Groell's Suvudu Q&A
claims.quote: most of which was back-checking information from previous books

claims.claim: Pajiba reports that three battles were cut from A Dance With Dragons for length and for writing time.
claims.source: Genevieve Burgess, Pajiba (2014-05-30), relaying Anne Groell's Suvudu Q&A
claims.quote: Three battles were cut from A Dance With Dragons

claims.claim: Pajiba reports that Martin was stubborn about keeping the repeated phrase his editor wanted cut.
claims.source: Genevieve Burgess, Pajiba (2014-05-30), relaying Anne Groell's Suvudu Q&A

claims.claim: MoPOP headlines its Martin oral-history clip with Martin's remark that he always knew they were summer snows, an image he says he had from the beginning.
claims.source: Museum of Pop Culture blog (2019-04-16), quoting George R.R. Martin's MoPOP oral history
claims.quote: I always knew they were summer snows

claims.claim: The MoPOP blog says Martin's philosophy of two types of writers is delivered in the clip with poetic imagery that is almost like listening to a parable.
claims.quote: so much poetic imagery it’s almost like listening to a parable
